record.original_question: For an irreducible Markov modulated Poisson process (MMPP), is the squared coefficient of variation of the event-stationary inter-event time always at least 1? Equivalently, if T_1^alpha denotes the first inter-event time in the event-stationary version of the process, must c^2 = Var(T_1^alpha) / E[T_1^alpha]^2 satisfy c^2 >= 1 for every irreducible MMPP?

evidence.quote: Consider the squared coefficient of variation and the limiting index of dispersion of counts given by, c^2 = Var(T_1^alpha) / E^2[T_1^alpha], and d^2 = lim_{t->infty} Var(N(t)) / E[N(t)], where T_1^alpha is the time of the first event, taken from the event stationary version.
Conjecture 4.1. For an irreducible MMPP, c^2 >= 1.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\{X(t)\}_{t\ge 0}$ be a continuous-time, irreducible, finite-state Markov chain on a state space $S=\{1,\dots,n\}$ with generator matrix $Q$ and unique stationary distribution $\pi$. Let $\Lambda=\mathrm{diag}(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n)$ with $\lambda_i\ge 0$ and at least one $\lambda_i>0$. Conditional on the trajectory of $X(\cdot)$, let $N(\cdot)$ be an inhomogeneous Poisson process with instantaneous rate $\lambda_{X(t)}$; the pair $(X(\cdot),N(\cdot))$ is called an irreducible Markov modulated Poisson process (MMPP). Let $0<T_1<T_2<\dots$ denote the event epochs of $N$, and let $T_k^\alpha=T_k-T_{k-1}$ (with $T_0=0$) denote the inter-event times under the event-stationary distribution (the Palm distribution at event epochs, equivalently the stationary distribution of the embedded chain $X(T_k-)$ at event times). Define the squared coefficient of variation
$$c^2 \;=\; \frac{\mathrm{Var}(T_1^\alpha)}{(\mathbb{E}[T_1^\alpha])^2}.$$
Prove or disprove: for every irreducible MMPP, $c^2 \ge 1$.
artifact.status_search_result: A 2018 manuscript titled "The Squared Coefficient of Variation for MMPP is Greater than Unity" (arXiv:1802.08400) provides a proof that for any irreducible MMPP, the squared coefficient of variation of the event-stationary inter-event time satisfies c^2 ≥ 1, together with an associated stochastic order relation. The conjecture therefore appears to be resolved affirmatively.

status_evidence.title: The Squared Coefficient of Variation for MMPP is Greater than Unity
status_evidence.snippet: Proof that for irreducible MMPPs the squared coefficient of variation of the event-stationary inter-event time is at least one.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture c^2 >= 1 for irreducible MMPPs has been proved.
